media.title: Max Ophüls — Studio Harcourt portrait, 1950s
media.altText: Black-and-white studio portrait of the film director Max Ophüls by Studio Harcourt.
media.publicCaption: Max Ophüls photographed by Studio Harcourt in the 1950s — later than the work documented here. Ophüls directed On a volé un homme (1934), the French film for which Kaper wrote the music.
media.publicCreditLine: Studio Harcourt / Réunion des musées nationaux — Grand Palais, via Wikimedia Commons.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared, and the release recorded on the Wikimedia Commons file is not relied on here. The file states that Studio Harcourt and the French government released the photograph into the public domain, citing VRT ticket 2020112910005534, but the same ticket is cited on the Commons files of the Harcourt portraits of Joséphine Baker (1940) and Henri-Georges Clouzot (1947) for a different claim: that Harcourt photographs are collective works whose French term runs seventy years from publication. Read that way, a portrait of the 1950s was still protected in France on 1 January 1996, so the URAA restored United States copyright for ninety-five years from publication. The archive treats the three Harcourt portraits alike. The photograph dates from the 1950s and is used only to identify Max Ophüls; it does not document the 1902–1939 chronology.
